title: Tendulkar Names Ganguly and Dhoni His Favourite Captains, Recalls a 'Dark Phase'
excerpt: At a Kolkata book event, Sachin Tendulkar praised Ganguly's fearlessness and Dhoni's understanding — and said the years between them were lost to poor planning, not lack of talent.
body:
• Asked at a Kolkata book event to name his favourite captain, Sachin Tendulkar picked two: Sourav Ganguly and MS Dhoni.
  • On Ganguly: "Sourav was fearless and took responsibility in tough situations." On Dhoni: "I did not need to say anything because he understood everything."
  • Tendulkar also recalled a "dark phase" between the two eras: "We did not lose matches because of lack of talent, but because of lack of planning and execution."
  • Across a 24-year career he played under six India captains, including Mohammad Azharuddin, Rahul Dravid and Anil Kumble.

Sachin Tendulkar played under six India captains across 24 years. Asked to pick a favourite, he picked two — and explained each in a single sentence. Speaking at a book event in Kolkata on Tuesday for Boria Majumdar's What If: The Life and Times of Sachin Ramesh Tendulkar, Tendulkar named Sourav Ganguly and MS Dhoni as the captains he most enjoyed playing under, according to NDTV Sports and Rediff.

"My favourite captains are Sourav Ganguly and MS Dhoni. Sourav was fearless and took responsibility in tough situations."

— Sachin Tendulkar, in Kolkata

Two captains, two qualities

On Ganguly, Tendulkar pointed to nerve and ownership. "My favourite captains are Sourav Ganguly and MS Dhoni. Sourav was fearless and took responsibility in tough situations," he said. He recalled Ganguly's dressing-room management with similar economy: "Sourav always knew how to create a good atmosphere in the dressing room." On Dhoni, the praise was about understanding rather than instruction: "With Dhoni, I did not need to say anything because he understood everything. He is calm under pressure and makes good decisions when it matters most."

The 'dark phase' in between

Tendulkar was equally direct about the years that separated the two tenures he praised. "Indian cricket went through a dark phase in between," he said. "We did not lose matches because of lack of talent, but because of lack of planning and execution." Pressed on the same theme, he returned to it: "Talent was always there, but the planning was not right." The remark points to the years that separated the two tenures he praised, though Tendulkar named no names and attached it to no single series or coach.

The roll of honour

The question has a long answer sheet. Across his career Tendulkar played under Mohammad Azharuddin, Ganguly, Rahul Dravid, Anil Kumble and Dhoni — and captained India himself. That he reached past his own era to name the captain who rebuilt India's self-belief and the captain who converted it into World Cup wins is a tidy summary of how Indian cricket remembers those years — and, from the man who played through all of it, a verdict with some weight.
